chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazalah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father was saying that for the Ablution (Wudu) there is a Limit. The one who exceeds it would not be recompensed; and my father was saying: 'But rather, he would be bewildered'. So a man said to him, 'And what is its Limit?' He said: 'You should wash your face, and your hands, and wipe your head and your feet'.
ai.seo_question: What is the defined limit for ritual ablution (Wudu) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the prominent Shaykh al-Kulayni, clarifies the jurisprudential boundary (hadd) of Wudu, warning that excessive washing beyond the obligatory limbs yields no additional spiritual reward. It highlights the Imams' emphasis on moderation (wasatiyyah) in ritual practice, distinguishing between the essential acts of washing the face and hands and wiping the head and feet, thereby preventing unnecessary rigorism.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abu Dawood, altogether from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Myasws fatherasws was saying that for the Ablution (Wudhu) there is a Limit. The one who exceeds it would not be Recompensed; and myasws fatherasws was saying: ‘But rather, he would be bewildered’. So a man said to himasws, ‘And what is its Limit?’ Heasws said: ‘You should wash your face, and your hands, and wipe your head and your feet’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and abu Dawud all from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘My father would say, “Wudu 5 has certain limits. If one trespasses such limits, he will not receive any reward.” My father would also say, “(Certain people) only make it perplexed.’” A man then asked, ‘What then are the limits of Wudu’?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Wash your face and hands and wipe your head and feet.’”
